transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-16
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nandakumar (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (InsightBridge - Head of Platform), Jared Voss (InsightBridge - SRE), Lena Ortiz (InsightBridge - Product), Tom (DevOps)
---
Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be imperfect): Quick console walkthrough focused on per-route usage analytics, attribution to teams, and cost breakdown. Customer wants to validate Redwood Console's route-level telemetry and how it maps to their billing. Discussed hosted vs dedicated, VPC considerations, retention, and SSO/audit logs. Action items and follow-ups listed.
Topics: 1) Route attribution model 2) Cost breakdown per route 3) Data retention/encryption 4) Pilot scope and next steps
---
Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm alex from redwood, i'll kick us off. um priya will run the console demo after a quick discovery.
[00:18] Maya: hey alex hi priya thanks. we're excited — we want to see per-route cost so our product owners can see bill impact per feature flag.
[00:28] Alex: great quick qual question, what does your current stack look like for inference? are you calling us via API gateway or directly through an internal endpoint?
[00:40] Maya: right now we run a mix. internal services call models in our infra — mostly on prem GPUs for heavy jobs, and we also call a managed endpoint from one of the clouds for burst. lots of routes; some routes are dev-only.
[00:55] Priya: when you say routes, is that at the API route level or per-feature bucket? how are you tagging traffic today?
[01:06] Jared: we use headers and route names in our gateway. not everything is tagged though; older services don't include the route header.
[01:15] Alex: okay that maps well to Redwood's per-route dashboard — you can attach a route id or token on the request and console will attribute tokens/calls to that route, even break down tokens vs embeddings.
[01:34] Lena: curious on the billing side — can we map route to internal chargeback to teams? our finance folks want daily exports.
[01:44] Priya: yes we have per-route exports and a billing CSV that splits by model, route, tokens in, tokens out, and cost estimate; there's also a delta vs real spend table for reserved capacity.
[01:59] Tom: one quick security note — we need to keep data in our VPC, and KMS keys are mandatory.
[02:09] Alex: totally — Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and VPC connectors; we also provide audit logs and SAML SSO for RBAC. i'll point you to the security pack after.
[02:22] Maya: do you have SOC 2 or ISO?
[02:26] Priya: yes SOC 2 type II, and we have an ISO roadmap for next quarter — i'll share the certs in the follow-up.
[02:35] Jared: performance question: if we enable per-route attribution and caching, will it impact latency? we have a 100ms p95 SLO.
[02:46] Priya: good question — the attribution is a metadata layer in the control plane, it doesn't change serving kernels. cache hits (KV cache) are inline; we do continuous batching but can keep sub-200ms p95 for many models. sometimes transcription shows "K V cash" in older notes, ignore that.
[03:05] Alex: ok priya will jump into the live console — show route overview, then per-route token breakdown and the export.
[03:12] Priya: sharing screen now — here's the Redwood Consolet home (note: transcript may call it consolet or console). first panel is 'Usage Lens' which is the per-route ingress view.
[03:30] [screen share noise] Priya: at the top you can change time window — last 24h, 7d, or custom. in this example we filter by project and then by route tag. you can see request count, avg tokens, cost estimate.
[03:52] Maya: can you show how it handles model rollouts? we often switch from an Llama-variant to quantized variant.
[04:01] Priya: sure — notice model column; rerouting is handled by the runtime. console will show model versions and you can compare per-route metrics across versions (latency, cost). here's an example where a quantized variant cut cost 35% but added 8ms p95.
[04:26] Jared: is that a hard cost number or an estimate? our chargeback must match our billing closely.
[04:32] Priya: the console shows estimates derived from runtime token unit costs plus reserved capacity allocation. we also provide raw billing export so finance can reconcile against the invoice.
[04:46] Alex: for Dedicated setups, there's a different allocation method; we'll show a worked example in the pilot.
[04:54] Maya: retention — how long do you keep route-level telemetry? some of our product data is PII-ish so we need short retention and redaction options.
[05:06] Priya: retention is configurable per-project; you can set route telemetry to 30/90/365 days. for PII you can enable payload redaction and only keep headers/metrics. all logs can be pushed to your audit endpoint too.
[05:25] Tom: and encryption in transit + at rest? KMS?
[05:29] Alex: yes TLS in transit — customer-managed KMS for at-rest for Private. Hosted offers envelope encryption and we integrate with major cloud KMS.
[05:40] [06:00] Priya: switch to 'Route Explorer' — this is the deep dive. you can see a heatmap per hour of tokens, and a waterfall shows token vs embedding usage per route.
[06:18] Priya: note: the chart labels sometimes truncate long service names, we recommend short route ids for readability.
[06:26] Maya: can we link a route to a jira or a team id? finance wants team mapping.
[06:33] Priya: yes there's a mapping table; you can assign a route to a cost center or a team id and that flows into the export. we support a small API to manage mappings programmatically.
[06:45] Jared: about sample rate — we have high volume routes. does sampling throw off cost?
[06:50] Priya: sampling in analytics only — billing exports still use raw request counts. sampling is optional to reduce telemetry storage.
[07:01] Alex: at ~10 minutes let's show an example export — Priya can click 'export billing CSV'.
[07:10] Priya: exporting now — fields: timestamp, route_id, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, estimated_cost, team_id, region. you can also include request_id for tracing.
[07:24] Lena: that's perfect. we need daily dumps into our data lake. can you push to S3/GCS?
[07:31] Priya: yes you can schedule exports to S3 or GCS; for Private you can push to your internal endpoint.
[07:40] Jared: about burst credits — we may want to keep base reserved capacity and burst to hosted. how is that shown in console?
[07:50] Priya: the capacity page shows allocation per pool; when a route hits dedicated threshold you get fallbacks in the runtime and console shows 'burst usage' and the associated delta cost.
[08:03] Maya: compliance — any red flags for us to share with legal?
[08:10] Alex: we'll send the security pack; main items are SOC2, SAML/SSO, KMS integration, and audit log retention options. for on-prem we also have an air-gapped package.
[08:22] [08:40] Priya: demo — 'Cost Breakdown' tab: you can split cost by route, model, and team. here's a pivot where we assigned team tag and see team A using 62% of tokens this week.
[08:55] Priya: there's also an anomaly detector that flags unexpected token spikes and can alert to slack/email.
[09:05] Jared: how noisy is that? false positives are rough for us.
[09:10] Priya: you tune sensitivity per alert and define blackout windows. we also support baselining using previous 30 days.
[09:22] Maya: back to privacy — any payload indexing? we don't want raw prompts stored.
[09:29] Priya: by default prompts are not indexed; you can enable ephemeral logging for troubleshooting which expires. redaction options exist to remove PII before storage.
[09:43] Tom: will route attribution work for async jobs (batch)? we have long-run batch inference.
[09:51] Priya: yes we tag batch jobs and the console shows batch vs streaming; token accounting is the same. for KV cache warmups it's slightly different but we surface warmup as a distinct line item.
[10:10] Alex: quick pause — any blockers to run a pilot?
[10:16] Maya: two: (1) need to verify retention & redaction for legal, (2) need sample billing to reconcile with finance.
[10:25] Alex: both noted. we'll send certs and a sample billing export.
[10:32] [10:50] Priya: let's show a model comparison view — here you can pick two model versions and diff latency/cost per route. this is handy during canary rollouts.
[11:08] Priya: small gotcha: if you use heavy quantization some reward-model outputs change slightly; console ties model changes to quality metrics if you push evaluation sets.
[11:22] Lena: do you track hallucination/regression metrics? we have a critical eval suite.
[11:28] Priya: yes we integrate eval sets; console shows regression alerts when response quality drops vs baseline. you can attach example prompts so product teams see the regression.
[11:46] Jared: network — we need egress considerations. if console pushes logs to S3, will egress cost be visible?
[11:55] Priya: egress is out-of-band; console will show estimated regional egress but final bill is from your cloud provider. we can approximate in the export though.
[12:10] Alex: shifting to pilot scope — proposed steps: 1) sandbox + quickstart 2) pilot with 3 routes (one high volume, one batch, one dev) 3) reconcile vs billing 4) decide Dedicated or Hosted.
[12:27] Maya: timeline? we target a decision in 6 weeks due to Q3 planning.
[12:32] Alex: doable — pilot could be 2 weeks of data then a sync.
[12:40] Priya: i'll share a checklist for the pilot: route tagging, sample export, API keys, sandbox creds, and security assessment.
[12:52] [13:10] Maya: curious about tagging overhead — does it require code changes for each service?
[13:18] Priya: minimal — you add a header or set route param in SDK. for legacy apps you can map gateway routes to Redwood route ids without code change.
[13:32] Tom: will mapping add latency?
[13:35] Priya: no measurable latency — mapping is done at the control plane and is asynchronous for analytics.
[13:44] Jared: what about high-cardinality routes? we have dozens per service.
[13:49] Priya: console handles high-cardinality but recommends grouping or short ids; the heatmaps get noisy otherwise.
[14:00] Alex: competitor question — any comparison notes to Anthropic or SageMaker? we often get asked.
[14:08] Priya: short answer: Redwood focuses on unified runtime + cost controls across hosted/dedicated/private; Anthropic is model-first, SageMaker is infra-first. Redwood's per-route economics and automatic KV caching are differentiators.
[14:28] Maya: and data residency? we need EU-only for some routes.
[14:33] Alex: you can pin routes to regions and console shows regional allocations; Private gives full control.
[14:44] [15:00] Priya: now walk through the 'Exports' config — you can schedule daily S3 pushes, include redaction rules, and set encryption options.
[15:16] Priya: for pilot we'll enable S3 export with encryption and a 30-day telemetry retention.
[15:25] Jared: will the export include request payloads?
[15:29] Priya: only if you opt in for troubleshooting; otherwise it's headers/metrics only.
[15:42] Maya: show me anomaly alert setup quickly.
[15:49] Priya: click Alerts -> New Rule, choose metric (tokens per min), set threshold or use baseline, then choose slack/email webhook.
[16:05] Tom: what's the retention of audit logs for SAML auth events?
[16:11] Alex: audit logs retention is configurable, by default 90 days for hosted; Private you manage retention.
[16:21] Lena: what about role-based access? can we limit route visibility by team?
[16:27] Priya: yes RBAC supports route-level permissions; you can restrict which teams see which routes and which exports.
[16:37] Maya: any latency introduced by RBAC checks?
[16:41] Priya: no, RBAC is enforced at the console and control plane for UI; runtime calls use tokens and route ids so no extra latency.
[16:53] Alex: roughly 30 minutes in, let's surface a few logs — Priya: open the audit log view.
[17:02] Priya: here's an example audit event: user X exported billing CSV, timestamp, and IP. you can download or forward to your SIEM.
[17:16] Jared: can we forward logs to Splunk?
[17:19] Priya: yes HTTP/S hookups for Splunk, Datadog, Sumo, or push to S3.
[17:31] Maya: any chance of double-counting when a route is proxied through multiple gateways?
[17:38] Priya: there are dedupe options: request-id or client-generated uuid will dedupe to avoid double-counts.
[17:50] Alex: let's talk pilot success criteria — what should we measure?
[17:55] Maya: (1) reconciliation within 2% of invoice (2) ability to produce daily exports (3) retention/privacy verified by legal (4) demonstration of cost-savings path (quantized variant)
[18:13] Priya: noted. we'll add quality metrics and a small eval harness to track regressions.
[18:22] [18:40] Tom: if we go Dedicated, what's the provisioning lead time?
[18:45] Alex: depends on region and capacity — typical is 2-6 weeks for reserved pools; for pilot we suggest hosted with dedicated plan option later.
[18:58] Jared: what's your SLA for Dedicated?
[19:02] Alex: 99.9% with latency SLOs agreed in contract. we'll provide the SLA doc.
[19:12] Maya: about cost — can you show an example where route-level optimization saved money?
[19:17] Priya: yes, example case: a customer moved batch preprocessing to quantized offline model and reduced per-token cost 40% and overall monthly spend 18% by using KV caching and model selection per route.
[19:36] Lena: can Optimize recommend quantization automatically?
[19:40] Priya: Redwood Optimize provides suggestions, but we usually validate with an eval set for quality vs cost tradeoff.
[19:52] Alex: minute 40 — any outstanding security or procurement items?
[19:59] Maya: legal will want the SOC2 and redaction proof. procurement wants pilot T&C and an NDA.
[20:06] Alex: we have an NDA template and pilot T&C — i'll attach them in the follow-up.
[20:14] Priya: quick demo note — we'll create a sandbox org for you and pre-populate 3 routes to speed pilot.
[20:25] Jared: please include a sample S3 export so finance can do a dry run.
[20:31] Alex: yep, that's in the action items.
[20:38] [21:00] Maya: timeline recap — we want the pilot started by end of month.
[21:06] Alex: we'll aim to get sandbox creds and docs by 2025-07-17. pilot kickoff next week if all aligns.
[21:16] Priya: i'll also add a checklist for the SREs: header mapping, route ids, sample CSV format, and retention settings.
[21:28] Tom: ok thanks — last question: do you support function/tool calling telemetry? our app does function calls triggered by models so we'd like to see cost per tool.
[21:38] Priya: yes we surface tool/function calls as separate line items in the export and console graph. you can group them as needed.
[21:50] Lena: great, that covers most of our questions.
[22:00] [22:20] Alex: cool, quick recap and next steps: 1) Alex send pricing + billing export + NDA + security pack (by 2025-07-18), 2) Priya share sandbox + quickstart + sample notebook (by 2025-07-17), 3) Jared provide traffic samples and retention needs (by 2025-07-20), 4) schedule pilot kickoff (tentative week of 2025-07-28).
[22:45] Maya: thanks all — we'll review with legal and finance and confirm pilot scope.
[22:52] Alex: thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email — appreciate the time.
[23:00] [End of recording - approximate]
---
Notes: Transcript contains typical ASR imperfections (mis-attributed speaker tags, minor word swaps). Shared artifacts referenced: https://redwood.ai/docs/console-route-insights ; sample billing export (attached by Alex after call) ; NDA and security pack (to be shared).
